data.description:
## Context
The completion-verifier sidecar now attributes wrapper time without a residual, but the largest inner interval is still exposed only as `workflow_ms`. That label hides the operations responsible for hundreds of seconds and cannot support performance diagnosis or expectation-setting.

## Plan
- Trace the completion workflow call path and define concrete, non-overlapping subphase boundaries whose sum explains `workflow_ms`.
- Add monotonic duration measurements at existing seams only; instrumentation must not add LLM calls, Git work, filesystem snapshots, network requests, retries, or other material work.
- Emit the named subphase durations in the completion sidecar while preserving existing aggregate fields and compatibility with older sidecars.
- Extend the reusable duration probe to display and validate the new workflow breakdown and surface any remaining workflow residual explicitly.
- Add focused automated coverage for metric emission, partition arithmetic, and legacy sidecars; rely on CI for execution because local resources are limited.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `workflow_ms` is broken into concrete operation-named, non-overlapping subphase durations.
- [ ] The subphase durations plus an explicit residual reconcile to `workflow_ms` within documented rounding tolerance.
- [ ] Instrumentation performs only in-process monotonic clock reads and sidecar field construction; it adds no LLM, Git, filesystem snapshot, network, retry, or subprocess work.
- [ ] Existing aggregate fields remain available and older sidecars remain parseable by the reusable probe.
- [ ] CI coverage verifies emission and arithmetic for the new fields and compatibility for old records.
- [ ] The final ticket record explains what each formerly generic workflow interval contains.
data.title: Break down completion verifier workflow timing into concrete subphases
